A1.justification: Both PDFs describe STARCaster, with matching authors, architecture, tasks and core experiments. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original portrait-animation and novel-view experiments, component ablations, a user study and qualitative results, including supplementary examples.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds runtime measurements, further comparisons, an additional ablation and qualitative diagnostic analyses.

M1.justification: The stated inference rule gains independently adjustable audio and camera attention weights in [0,1] (v2 Section 3.1, Equation 1), whereas v1 Equation 2 specifies an unweighted sum. This is a limited extension of described conditioning control. The backbone, reference network, objectives, three training stages and F=2 recursion remain; additional implementation explanations do not establish further method changes.

E1.justification: Training sources and quantitative benchmarks remain unchanged: VFHQ, CelebV-HQ, HDTF, synthetic heads, TH-1KH, Hallo3 and NeRSemble. Qualitative viewpoint-control coverage expands to accessory-heavy inputs, notably sunglasses and hats, in v2 Figure 13 and Appendix A.2.1, replacing the simpler examples in v1 Figure 7. This is a limited input-condition extension.

E2.justification: EDTalk is added to the evaluated portrait-animation comparators in Table 1 and Figure 4. The other portrait-animation baselines and the three NeRSemble comparators remain. The new runtime comparison evaluates an existing subset: V-Express, EchoMimic, AniPortrait and Hallo3.

E3.justification: Evaluation expands through several substantive protocol additions. The user study changes from 20 participants evaluating 15 sample sets to 35 evaluating 25; NeRSemble gains LSE-C/LSE-D metrics. New protocols measure A100 runtime for five-second, 25-FPS clips, replace the first two training stages with one for an ablation, and inspect reconstructions across noise levels. Existing benchmark sampling and full-model training schedules are retained.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained lip-reading and self-forcing ablations, v2 tests progressive training by removing its staged structure (Table 4). It adds modality-specific attention analysis (Section 4.3, Figure 7), a qualitative single-step reconstruction check across four noise levels (Figure 11), and challenging viewpoint-control examples. These substantially broaden design and mechanism validation, although the reconstruction check uses one illustrated frame.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, random-seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests. The identity-similarity distribution is retained. Pose Std measures generated head-motion diversity, not estimation uncertainty; increasing the user-study sample changes evaluation design rather than uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Retained benchmark and original ablation values are unchanged, but substantial results are added: EDTalk scores, NeRSemble lip-sync scores, runtime measurements and the progressive-training ablation. STARCaster's new NeRSemble LSE-C/LSE-D values are 3.957/7.952; runtime is 2.2 minutes versus Hallo3's 21.4. Figure 6 preferences change from 31/26/23/20% to 32/27/22/19% for Ours/Hallo3/EchoMimic/FLOAT under the enlarged study, not identical conditions. New qualitative diagnostics also extend the reported findings.

T1.justification: The cross-attention definition is generalized from an unweighted sum in v1 Equation 2 to independently weighted audio and camera contributions in v2 Equation 1. Otherwise, the mathematical setup is retained. Removing the standard softmax-attention equation is expository; neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The unified identity-, audio- and view-conditioned contribution remains. v2 refines the abstract's free-viewpoint-synthesis framing to dynamic viewpoint control and replaces the introduction's explicit state-of-the-art cross-view-coherence assertion with a non-ranking claim of excellent coherence. The broader benchmark-superiority narrative remains.

C2.justification: Beyond the existing slow-inference and background-animation caveats, v2 explicitly excludes rear views and 360-degree coverage and discusses skin smoothing and color inconsistencies associated with synthetic-data adaptation. New attention interpretations explain modality localization and acknowledge non-identity information in identity embeddings and the approximate nature of attention visualizations. These materially clarify mechanisms and applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1 newly documents camera conventions, field of view and initial-pose estimation; reference-network weight sharing and additional parameter counts; modality dropout at p=0.05; and single-step denoising for auxiliary supervision and recursion. It also explains 60% latent crops, framewise VAE slicing and lip-reader memory costs. These substantially improve implementation documentation without establishing changed training runs. The project URL remains, while the direct InsightFace repository link is removed.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Ho et al.'s Video Diffusion Models and Tan et al.'s EDTalk, while removing the Sora 2, Veo 3 and Isambard-AI references. Appendix A.1.3 adds explicit positioning of the frozen, shared reference network against trainable reference networks. Most related-work coverage remains; author-year citations and publication-metadata updates are presentation changes.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order are largely retained, with targeted rewrites, clearer explanations and more consistent self-forcing-based terminology. An attention-analysis subsection is inserted, the appendix is reorganized into implementation and qualitative-results subsections, and the social-impact note moves before the references. This is a limited editorial restructuring rather than a wholesale rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a substantially different conference layout with running headers, revised title and affiliation placement, and widespread figure/table reflow. It adds a runtime table, attention maps and reconstruction diagnostics; expands comparison tables and Figure 4; and replaces the main-text viewpoint gallery with different appendix examples. Retained supplementary galleries are relocated and renumbered, rather than wholly new.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens an already empirically supported paper through the progressive-training ablation, measured runtime, clearer implementation instructions and explicit viewpoint and artifact limitations. These additions improve reproducibility and calibrate the claims. The gain is incremental: core benchmark results remain unchanged, several new checks are qualitative, and uncertainty reporting is not improved.
